chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, raising it (mursal), said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed I dislike it for the man that a bounty from God be upon him, yet he does not manifest it.'

key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: he raised it (mursal/marfu' — the chain is elevated past the intermediate narrator)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about displaying God's blessings?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expressed disapproval of concealing God's blessings. In classical Islamic thought, being bestowed a divine bounty — whether health, wealth, knowledge, or piety — carries with it an obligation to display and acknowledge it as a form of gratitude (shukr) to God. This teaching is transmitted via a mursal chain through Ibn Abi Umayr, one of the most trusted Shia narrators. The original audience would have understood 'manifest the bounty' as including both acknowledging it verbally (by praising God) and making appropriate use of it in one's appearance and conduct.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, raising it, said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> dislike it for the man that a Bounty happens to be upon him from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so he does not manifest it’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr in a marfu‘ manner has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘I dislike to see a man who has received a bounty from Allah but does not show it."
